business_problem: Wrtn needed to move beyond narrow productivity tools and make AI feel natural, localized, and useful for everyday Korean users across creativity, learning, and conversation at mass scale.
solution_summary: Wrtn built a consumer AI stack that combines localized prompting, memory scaffolding, and model routing so millions of users can interact with AI in natural Korean rather than translated English patterns. Its Crack character-chat product and broader suite of AI Supporter and Labs experiences sit on top of a router architecture that sends lightweight classification and traffic-direction tasks to GPT-4o mini and GPT-4.1 mini, while heavier tutoring, counseling, and multimodal interactions run on GPT-4.1, GPT-5, and audio models. Persona prompts, role guidance, and temperature tuning shape the tone and pacing of responses, while each new OpenAI release can be swapped into the stack with minimal disruption. That architecture let Wrtn improve retention, time spent, and localization quality while scaling lifestyle AI across Korea and into new East Asian markets.

data_flow: User requests enter Crack or other Wrtn apps, where the router architecture classifies intent with smaller models and sends heavier work to GPT-4.1, GPT-5, or multimodal audio paths. Persona prompts, memory scaffolding, and localization layers shape the response before the product returns text or voice output to the user.
business_outcome: Wrtn reached 6.5 million monthly active users, doubled retention, quadrupled time spent per user, and used same-day GPT-5 adoption plus a modular model router to keep improving consumer engagement and localization quality.
